claims.text: What the image looks like Round/oval hyperdensity within parenchyma → intraparenchymal hemorrhage
claims.quote: Round/oval hyperdensity within parenchyma Intraparenchymal hemorrhage

claims.text: Example noncontrast CT: increased density in the left brain, consistent with intracerebral hemorrhage
claims.quote: Increased density in the left brain seen on this noncontrast CT is consistent with intracerebral hemorrhage.

claims.text: Intracerebral hemorrhages commonly occur in the thalamus and within the basal ganglia
claims.quote: This CT scan shows a hemorrhage in the thalamus. Intracerebral hemorrhages commonly occur in the thalamus and within the basal ganglia.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Confirm it is non-contrast (so blood/calcium is not confused with contrast)
claims.quote: Confirm non-contrast (so blood/calcium not confused with contrast).

claims.text: Symmetry: gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns
claims.quote: Symmetry - gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns.

claims.text: Blood: look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH)
claims.quote: Blood - look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH).

claims.text: Brain: gray-white preservation; look for sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift
claims.quote: Brain - gray-white preservation, sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift.

claims.text: Cisterns: basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk
claims.quote: Cisterns - basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk.

claims.text: Ventricles: symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus
claims.quote: Ventricles - symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus.

claims.text: Rupture into the ventricular system (intraventricular hemorrhage) may cause acute hydrocephalus, an independent predictor of worse outcome
claims.quote: If the hemorrhage ruptures into the ventricular system (intraventricular hemorrhage), blood may cause acute hydrocephalus, an independent predictor for a worse outcome after intracerebral hemorrhage.

claims.text: CTA within hours of onset may show contrast extravasating into the clot (spot sign): this indicates bleeding is continuing and suggests the hematoma will expand and the outcome will be poor
claims.quote: CT angiography (CTA), performed within hours of bleeding onset, may show areas where contrast extravasates into the clot (spot sign); this finding indicates that bleeding is continuing and suggests that the hematoma will expand and the outcome will be poor.

claims.text: Causes Her chart: HTN (basal ganglia); amyloid angiopathy (lobar); AVM
claims.quote: Intraparenchymal hemorrhage (HTN basal ganglia; amyloid angiopathy lobar; AVM)

claims.text: Usually rupture of an arteriosclerotic small artery weakened primarily by chronic arterial hypertension; such hemorrhages are usually large, single and catastrophic
claims.quote: Intracerebral hemorrhage usually results from rupture of an arteriosclerotic small artery that has been weakened, primarily by chronic arterial hypertension. Such hemorrhages are usually large, single, and catastrophic.

claims.text: Chronic hypertension forms microaneurysms (Charcot-Bouchard aneurysms) in small perforating arteries, which may rupture
claims.quote: Chronic arterial hypertension leads to formation of microaneurysms (Charcot-Bouchard aneurysms) in small perforating arteries which may rupture and cause intracerebral hemorrhage.

claims.text: Lobar hemorrhages (in the cerebral lobes, outside the basal ganglia) usually result from cerebral amyloid angiopathy, which affects primarily older adults; they may be multiple and recurrent
claims.quote: Lobar intracerebral hemorrhages (hematomas in the cerebral lobes, outside the basal ganglia) usually result from angiopathy due to amyloid deposition in cerebral arteries (cerebral amyloid angiopathy), which affects primarily older adults. Lobar hemorrhages may be multiple and recurrent.

claims.text: Less often: congenital aneurysm, arteriovenous malformations, other vascular malformations, trauma, mycotic aneurysm, hemorrhagic infarction, primary or metastatic brain tumor, excessive anticoagulation, blood dyscrasia, intracranial arterial dissection, Moyamoya disease, or a bleeding or vasculitic disorder
claims.quote: Less often, intracerebral hemorrhage results from congenital aneurysm, arteriovenous malformations, other vascular malformations, trauma, mycotic aneurysm, brain infarct (hemorrhagic infarction), primary or metastatic brain tumor, excessive anticoagulation, blood dyscrasia, intracranial arterial dissection, Moyamoya disease, or a bleeding or vasculitic disorder.

claims.text: Cocaine or, occasionally, other sympathomimetic drugs can cause transient severe hypertension leading to hemorrhage
claims.quote: Use of cocaine or, occasionally, other sympathomimetic drugs or medications can cause transient severe hypertension leading to hemorrhage.

claims.text: Symptoms Typically begins with sudden headache, often during activity (it may be mild or absent in older adults); loss of consciousness is common, often within seconds or a few minutes; nausea, vomiting, delirium and focal or generalized seizures are also common
claims.quote: Symptoms of intracerebral hemorrhage typically begin with sudden headache, often during activity. However, headache may be mild or absent in older adults. Loss of consciousness is common, often within seconds or a few minutes. Nausea, vomiting, delirium, and focal or generalized seizures are also common.

claims.text: Neurologic deficits are usually sudden and progressive; large hemorrhages in the hemispheres cause hemiparesis
claims.quote: Neurologic deficits are usually sudden and progressive. Large hemorrhages, when located in the hemispheres, cause hemiparesis

claims.text: Small hemorrhages may cause focal deficits without impaired consciousness and with minimal or no headache and nausea; they may mimic ischemic stroke
claims.quote: Small hemorrhages may cause focal deficits without impairment of consciousness and with minimal or no headache and nausea. Small hemorrhages may mimic ischemic stroke.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: BP control; reverse anticoagulation; neurosurg consult
claims.quote: BP control; reverse anticoagulation; neurosurg consult

claims.text: Do CT or MRI and a bedside glucose test immediately
claims.quote: Do CT or MRI and a bedside glucose test immediately.

claims.text: Essential supportive care may include reversing anticoagulation and lowering BP to 140 mm Hg if systolic BP is between 150 and 220 mm Hg; if > 220 mm Hg, consider aggressive reduction with continuous IV nicardipine
claims.quote: Essential supportive care may include reversing anticoagulation and decreasing BP to 140 mm Hg if systolic BP is between 150 mm Hg and 220 mm Hg; if systolic BP is > 220 mm Hg, consider aggressively reducing BP by continuously infusing nicardipine IV.

claims.text: Avoid BP fluctuations, and maintain systolic BP < 140 mm Hg, but not lower than 130 mm Hg
claims.quote: Avoid BP fluctuations, and maintain systolic BP < 140 mm Hg, but not lower than 130 mm Hg.

claims.text: Anticoagulants and antiplatelets are contraindicated; reverse anticoagulant effects when possible with fresh frozen plasma, prothrombin complex concentrate, vitamin K or platelet transfusions as indicated; DOAC antidotes: idarucizumab (dabigatran), andexanet alfa (apixaban, rivaroxaban)
claims.quote: Anticoagulants and antiplatelet medications are contraindicated. If patients have used anticoagulants, the effects are reversed when possible by giving fresh frozen plasma, prothrombin complex concentrate, vitamin K, or platelet transfusions as indicated. Antidotes for direct oral anticoagulants are idarucizumab for dabigatran and andexanet alfa for apixaban and rivaroxaban.

claims.text: Early evacuation of large lobar hematomas may be lifesaving, but rebleeding occurs frequently; early evacuation of deep hematomas is seldom indicated (surgical mortality is high and deficits are usually severe)
claims.quote: Early evacuation of large lobar cerebral hematomas may also be lifesaving, but rebleeding occurs frequently, sometimes increasing neurologic deficits. Early evacuation of deep cerebral hematomas is seldom indicated because surgical mortality is high and neurologic deficits are usually severe.

claims.text: With hydrocephalus (a predictor of worse outcome), surgeons may place an external ventricular drain to rapidly lower ICP; this can be lifesaving
claims.quote: Because the presence of hydrocephalus predicts a worse outcome after intracerebral hemorrhage, surgeons may place an external ventricular drain to rapidly decrease intracranial pressure. This procedure can be lifesaving.

claims.text: Antiseizure medications are used only if the patient has had a seizure, not typically prophylactically
claims.quote: Antiseizure medications are used only if patients have had a seizure, but are not typically given prophylactically
